name: Cable reverse-grip curl
cue: Overhand grip, elbows at your sides; curl the bar up.
research: Standing cable curl with an overhand (pronated) grip on a straight bar (20 in, 0.285 H long, 25 mm thick, the grips about shoulder width apart) on a low pulley (0.075 H, in a fork on the column's base) in a column 0.5 H (0.9 m) in front of the stance, feet hip width, knees soft (6): the cable bar curl's stance and path with the forearms turned palms down. Design values from the standard technique description, not a measured trial: the elbows stay pinned at the sides (shoulder flexion 12 -> 14, so they drift about 2 deg forward at the top as the upper arm does; abduction about 3), the elbow flexes 20 -> 128 (not fully straight at the bottom so the fists clear the thighs), trunk still. Forearm pronation 170-175 (supination 0, neutral 90, the end of the forearm's range of about 80 deg past neutral), the wrists within 2 deg of neutral so the bar sits straight across the fists. The hands are fitted so the grip tunnel stays along the left-right axis (sagittal curl, tilt under 1.5 deg) and the bar passes through both fists (bone-attached on the hand, so it cannot slip; the ring on the bar's middle sits within 1 cm of the midline as the pronated hand turns); the cable is on the middle of the bar and leaves it 52 deg below horizontal at the bottom and 71 deg at the top (the moment arm against the cable, the sine of the angle between the forearm and the cable, is 0.22 of its maximum at the bottom, 0.84 at mid-range and 0.88 at the top). Cable 1:1 to the stack. Geometry: design/cableB/rc.mjs.

targets.note: design values (standard technique), not a measured trial

camera.note: The view of the hammer curl (az 60, el 12): the outer upper arm and the thumb side of the forearm face the camera, so the brachialis and the brachioradialis read as a band along the arm and a ridge along the forearm, and the cable shows where the load comes from. fitMachine false: the column may crop at the top.
